`scripts/testnet-smoke.mjs` is the end-to-end testnet check (`pnpm smoke`) and one of the few signals that the SDK works against live Circle Iris and real contracts. Public testnets and faucets flake constantly — transient RPC 5xx, attestation delays just over the poll window, faucet rate limits. A smoke script with no retry or step-level reporting turns every flake into a false alarm, and a script that doesn't exit non-zero on partial failure turns real breakage into a green-looking run.

**Proposed Change**
Restructure the script into named steps (fund/check, approve+burn, attestation wait, mint) with per-step retry + exponential backoff for infrastructure-shaped failures only (not for deterministic validation failures). Exit non-zero if any step ultimately fails, print a per-step pass/fail/duration summary at the end, and keep the burn hash printed prominently on post-burn failure so a human can recover the run with `completeMint`. No new dependencies — plain Node.

**Acceptance Criteria**

- Each step retries transient failures with backoff; deterministic failures (bad address, insufficient funds) fail immediately without retry.
- Final summary lists every step with status and duration; process exit code reflects overall outcome.
- Post-burn step failure prints the burn hash and the `completeMint` invocation needed to finish.
- Script remains runnable with existing env vars from `.env.example` / README smoke instructions.
- Verified by the `typecheck-test-build` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (script correctness reviewed manually; live run optional).

Nothing in the SDK accepts an `AbortSignal`. `pollForAttestation` (`src/iris/poll.ts:133-170`), `pollTransactionStatus` (`src/chains/stellar.ts:71-86`), and `waitForAllowance`/`retryOnTransientRpcLag` (`src/chains/stellar.ts:210-294`) all run `while` loops with fixed deadlines and no external cancellation. A service shutting down, a user navigating away from the demo, or a request-scoped timeout in a web backend cannot stop an in-flight transfer. This matters most after the burn: the README and `TransferError` docs promise the caller keeps `burnTxHash` for recovery, so an abort that discards it would violate the SDK's core safety contract.

**Proposed Change**
Thread an optional `signal?: AbortSignal` through `TransferOptionsBase` and `CompleteMintOptions`, honoring it in every polling/sleep loop (abortable sleep, not `setTimeout` fire-and-forget). Semantics: aborting before the burn throws a plain `AbortError` with nothing lost; aborting after the burn has been submitted throws a `TransferError` that still carries `burnTxHash` and sets `code` appropriately, so the recovery path is identical to any other post-burn failure. Fetches to Iris should pass the signal through.

- `transfer()` and `completeMint()` accept `options.signal` and the type surface compiles.
- Pre-burn abort rejects without submitting anything and without requiring recovery.
- Post-burn abort rejects with a `TransferError` whose `burnTxHash` is the real submitted hash.
- `pollForAttestation` aborts promptly (well before `pollTimeout`) and Iris `fetch` receives the signal.
- Tests cover pre-burn and post-burn abort with mocked chain calls.

A single transient RPC failure (connection reset, 5xx from the Soroban RPC) rejects the whole loop with whatever error the Stellar SDK threw — a bare error with no hash attached. Study **the entire book, lines 1–586**: 586 verse records in the [pinned Greek source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerseusDL/canonical-greekLit/ceeb60d9e9e0ebefd0f22b536e03a67084d2452a/data/tlg0012/tlg002/tlg0012.tlg002.perseus-grc2.xml), plus any properly evidenced supplements. Read the [project scope](https://github.com/mazebench-temp/GreekIndexBounty/blob/main/README.md), [research contract](https://github.com/mazebench-temp/GreekIndexBounty/blob/main/docs/research-standard.md), [submission format](https://github.com/mazebench-temp/GreekIndexBounty/blob/main/docs/submission-format.md), and [contribution guide](https://github.com/mazebench-temp/GreekIndexBounty/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). The 100,000-sat reward and direct payment terms in this issue replace the earlier 100-sat and Lightning Bounties setup terms wherever older repository documentation still shows them.

## Required delivery

- [ ] Verify and attribute the Greek source, numbering, rights, and any indirect witnesses.
- [ ] New careful line-aligned English translation of every submitted line, with recorded difficult decisions.
- [ ] Exact contextual lemma, gloss, and morphology for every Greek token occurrence.
- [ ] Complete scene, speech, speaker/addressee, and defensible narrative-day structure.
- [ ] Exhaustive line-by-line discovery of article candidates across all 18 kinds; research beyond obvious names.
- [ ] Shared researched articles and book-specific notes, correct identities/relations, concordance patterns, tags, precise citations, and stable quotes.
- [ ] Consulted-source log, candidate inventory with dispositions, all-category review, and coverage ledger.
- [ ] Separate translation, lexicon, index, source, and integration audits; findings resolved.
- [ ] New submission manifest and generated PR body disclosing actual models, runtime/settings, all subagents, time/tokens/cost or explicit unavailability, completeness/gaps, and evidence.
- [ ] Strict validation, tests, export, and rendered reader checks passed; maintainer scholarly/provenance review complete.

Investigate every line and every configured article category, including minor or implicit subjects, formulas, cultural practices, textual problems, and ancient reception. Follow relevant primary passages, lexica, commentaries, scholia, and scholarship beyond the obvious leads. Every candidate requires an evidenced disposition; there is no article quota or word-count target. Known unfinished work must be disclosed, never hidden behind a completion percentage. The sponsor’s approximate three-hour Iliad estimate is not a deadline, stopping rule, or substitute for the actual scope.

Ancient quotations and missing lines preserved in Aristotle, scholia, or other witnesses are encouraged. Use attributed witness records for numbered supplements and precise external citations for reception and testimonia; distinguish these from the base text.

## Eligibility and acceptance

Only **Anthropic Opus 5.5 or Fable 5.5** authorship is eligible, including every contributing writing or review agent. Report the actual provider/runtime model identifiers, reasoning effort and thinking settings, full agent roster and subagent count, timestamps, elapsed and aggregate agent time, token/cache usage, cost where available, completeness, remaining gaps, and audit evidence. Unknown telemetry is `null` with an explanation. Never relabel another model or invent an independent review. Private chain-of-thought is not requested.

Comment to request a claim; maintainer confirmation reserves it. Acceptance requires complete data and evidence, passing validation, and maintainer review of translation, scholarship, provenance, and reuse rights. One reward per accepted book; no duplicate or partial payment unless separately agreed. Payment of **100,000 sats** is arranged directly with the maintainer after acceptance and merge. Lightning Bounties registration and wallet connection are not submission requirements. No payment is triggered by CI, and no credentials or private payment information belong in GitHub.

```sh
npm run submission -- init odyssey-08
```

Run the checks in CONTRIBUTING.md, including strict manifest validation and the static export; inspect the reader, lexical sheets, article scopes, and quotes. Generate the PR description with `npm run --silent pr:body -- submissions/<UUID>.json`. Target `main`, retain exactly one manifest marker, and include `Closes` followed by the full URL of **this issue**. [!IMPORTANT]
> **⛔ TARGET BRANCH: `integration/staging` — open the fix PR against this branch, NOT `main`.**

**Problem**
Payment requests exist with amount, memo, due date and a shareable link plus a public invoice page (src/app/requests, src/app/pay/[address], /api/requests, and the RequestStatus enum in prisma/schema.prisma with its status lifecycle). What is missing is time-based behaviour: a request that passes its due date keeps displaying as outstanding, nothing notifies the requester when a request is paid or when it expires, and there is no way to send a reminder. Requests that silently go stale make the receivables view untrustworthy.

**Proposed improvement**
Add a scheduled transition that marks overdue requests and emits a webhook event and notification, a reminder action (rate-limited, with the number of reminders recorded), and clear overdue styling on the list and public page. Respect the notification preferences work rather than sending unconditionally.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A request past its due date is marked overdue automatically and visibly.
- Paid and overdue transitions emit webhook events and notifications exactly once.
- Reminders are rate-limited and counted, with the count visible to the requester.
- Tests cover the transition job and the reminder limits.

**Likely files:** src/app/api/requests/route.ts, src/lib/notifications.ts, prisma/schema.prisma, src/app/requests/page.tsx, src/app/pay/[address]/page.tsx

The signer already knows exactly what the fee was: `res.feeLamports`, taken from the confirmed transaction. It converts that to micro-USD using `solUsdCeilingPrice`, a deliberately high fixed SOL price ($400) chosen so the budget can never under-count spend.

That conversion is the only thing kept. `inference_calls` stores `fee_micro` and no lamports, so the ledger reports a conservative estimate and the exact figure is thrown away.

**Where in the code**

- `services/signer/src/signer.ts` — `PayResult` carries `fee_lamports`; look for `lamportsToMicroCeil(res.feeLamports, ...)`.
- `packages/x402/src/client.ts` — the settle call that records the payment drops `fee_lamports`.
- `db/migrations/` — add a new forward-only migration.

**What to do**

Carry `fee_lamports` through to the ledger and store it next to `fee_micro`.

Keep `fee_micro` exactly as it is. It uses the ceiling price on purpose so the budget stays conservative; this issue adds a factual column beside it, it does not change how spending is capped.

**How to verify**

- A new forward-only migration adds a nullable `fee_lamports` column to `inference_calls`. Existing rows are untouched and remain valid.
- A paid call records the lamports the transaction actually cost.
- A test proves `fee_micro` is unchanged for the same input.
- `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` pass.

## HER Hack-Astron #6 | Spark-X2.5 Math Reasoning Challenge

Put Spark-X2.5's mathematical reasoning to a real, honest, reproducible test.

For this challenge, obtain XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B or Spark-X2.5-1.7B from Hugging Face (or a mirror such as ModelScope), run a real math-reasoning evaluation or case study, and publish the complete, reproducible result in the corresponding model's Hugging Face Discussions. After publishing it, reply to this event's GitHub Issue with the Discussion link to enter.

- Event page (GitHub Issues): https://github.com/XHToken/Spark-X2.5/issues
- Hugging Face model collection: https://huggingface.co/collections/XHToken/spark-x25
- Spark-X2.5-4B: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B
- Spark-X2.5-1.7B: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B
- Spark-X2.5-4B Discussions: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B/discussions
- Spark-X2.5-1.7B Discussions: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B/discussions
- Mainland China mirror (recommended): https://www.modelscope.cn/collections/XHToken/Spark-X25

## FAQ Quick Summary

1. Solo participants of any gender are eligible.
2. The 50% women-contributor requirement applies only to teams.
3. AI-assisted and AI-operated evaluations are allowed when clearly disclosed.
4. Do not present AI personas as human participants.
5. Actual, reproducible model runs are required.
6. Formal submissions should follow the Hugging Face Discussion + GitHub Issue process.
7. International winners may use available payout methods such as PayPal or bank transfer.
8. Mainland China winners may coordinate RMB payout through an available domestic method.
9. No upfront fee is required.
10. Sensitive identity and payment information should only be provided privately if needed after winning.
11. No live presentation is currently required.

## Schedule

- Submissions open: September 7, 2026
- Challenge period: September 7–13, 2026
- Submission deadline: September 13, 2026, 24:00 Beijing Time (UTC+8)
- Judging and award distribution: September 14–20, 2026

## Challenge Tracks

Choose one track or combine several:

- Standard math benchmarks: evaluate on public sets such as GSM8K, MATH, MATH-500, AIME 2024/2025, OlympiadBench, or MinervaMath, and report pass@1 (and pass@k where relevant) with a clear scoring script
- Competition and olympiad problems: run AMC / AIME / IMO-style or national-olympiad problems and analyze where the model succeeds or fails
- Step-by-step reasoning quality: assess chain-of-thought correctness, not just final answers — catch right-answer-wrong-reasoning and arithmetic slips
- Tool-assisted math: combine the model with a code interpreter / Python / SymPy (program-aided reasoning) and compare against no-tool baselines
- Formal and proof-oriented math: theorem proving, proof sketching, or Lean/Coq-style formalization attempts, with honest reporting of verification
- Multilingual math: test math word problems and reasoning across languages (e.g. MGSM), and report per-language accuracy
- Robustness and contamination checks: perturbed / paraphrased / numerically-swapped problems, and evidence that results are not from memorized test data
- Decoding and prompting study: effect of temperature, self-consistency / majority voting, sampling budget, and prompt format on math accuracy — with cost trade-offs
- Comparative evaluation: compare Spark-X2.5 with larger models or other similar-size open models under one identical methodology

## How to Submit

1. Spark-X2.5 is licensed under Apache 2.0 and requires no additional usage agreement. Follow the repository's CODE_OF_CONDUCT and SECURITY policies.
2. Install and sign in with the official Hugging Face CLI:

       pip install -U huggingface_hub
       hf auth login

3. Download and record a pinned revision:

       hf download XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B --revision <commit-sha>

   Participants in Mainland China may use ModelScope / Modelers / SCNet / SourceFind mirrors. State the source and revision used.

4. Run a real math evaluation and retain publishable run logs, the exact command lines, the scoring/parsing script, raw model outputs, environment details, and screenshots.
5. Create a public post in the Discussions section for the model you actually used:

   - Spark-X2.5-1.7B: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B/discussions
   - Spark-X2.5-4B: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B/discussions

   The title only needs to contain `HER Hack-Astron #6`, for example:

       [HER Hack-Astron #6] <math evaluation title>

6. Reply to this event's GitHub Issue with the direct link to your Discussion post. This completes your submission. Examples:

       https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B/discussions/<number>
       https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B/discussions/<number>

## Acceptance Criteria

Every requirement below must be met for a submission to qualify:

1. **Real usage.** Provide the exact tested revision and sanitized snapshot/artifact information.
2. **Real execution.** Include the exact prompts, the dataset/version and split, representative problems, raw model outputs, and screenshot or log evidence.
3. **Required publication channel.** Publish the complete evaluation in the designated Spark-X2.5 Discussion. GitHub-only or other-platform-only submissions are not accepted.
4. **Reproducibility.** Record runtime versions (Transformers / vLLM / SGLang and image tags), hardware, precision/quantization, decoding parameters (temperature, top-p, max tokens, sampling count), the answer-extraction / scoring script, and the random seed.
5. **Honest metrics.** For any accuracy claim, report the dataset and split, number of problems, scoring method (exact match / equivalence checking), how ties or unparseable outputs are handled, and pass@1 vs pass@k or self-consistency settings.
6. **Reasoning integrity.** Do not report only final-answer accuracy on cherry-picked items; show representative full reasoning traces, including failures and wrong-reasoning-right-answer cases.
7. **Originality and licensing.** Use your own experiments and writing. State the license or authorization for any new data.
8. **Privacy and security.** Do not expose Hugging Face tokens, personal cache paths, private data, intranet addresses, or business data.
9. **No model-weight uploads.** Do not upload safetensors, GGUF, PT, PTH, or CKPT weight files to a Discussion or GitHub Issue reply. Publish GGUF files through Hugging Face or a mirror and provide only the download link.

For team entries, list all contributors in your GitHub Issue reply. At least 50% of the listed contributors must have profiles identifying them as women.

## Judging Criteria

- Real usage and execution evidence: 25%
- Reproducibility and technical completeness (scoring script, seeds, decoding settings): 25%
- Rigor and value of the math evaluation (dataset choice, contamination checks, methodology): 20%
- Honest metrics, reasoning-integrity and failure analysis: 20%
- Helpfulness of the Discussion post to future users: 10%

## HER Hack-Astron #5｜Spark-X2.5 端侧智能体真实使用案例挑战赛

把 Spark-X2.5 的真实运行过程沉淀为可复现、可讨论的端侧智能体案例。

本期挑战要求参与者从 Hugging Face（或 ModelScope 等镜像）获取 XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B 或 Spark-X2.5-1.7B，完成一次真实的推理、智能体、编码、长上下文、多语言、量化或训练实验，并把完整案例发布到对应模型的 Hugging Face Discussions。发布后，在本活动的 GitHub Issue 下回复 Discussion 链接即可参赛。

- 活动入口（GitHub Issues）：https://github.com/XHToken/Spark-X2.5/issues
- Hugging Face 模型集合：https://huggingface.co/collections/XHToken/spark-x25
- Spark-X2.5-4B：https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B
- Spark-X2.5-1.7B：https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B
- Spark-X2.5-4B Discussions：https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B/discussions
- Spark-X2.5-1.7B Discussions：https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B/discussions
- 国内镜像（推荐）：https://www.modelscope.cn/collections/XHToken/Spark-X25

## 赛程

- 开放提交：2026-09-01
- 赛事比拼：9 月 1 日–9 月 6 日
- 提交截止：2026 年 9 月 6 日 24:00（北京时间，UTC+8）
- 评奖与奖励发放：9 月 7 日–9 月 13 日

## 赛题方向

任选一个方向，也可以组合：

- 官方 Quick Start 复现：vLLM / SGLang / llama.cpp 部署，Ollama / LM Studio 本地运行，结构化输出与工具解析（`--tool-call-parser spark25`）
- 智能体工作流：接入 Codex、Claude Code、OpenClaw、Hermes 等 harness，完成多步工具调用、规划与自动化任务
- 编码能力：真实仓库级修复、竞赛/在线判题、代码代理端到端跑通
- 长上下文：利用原生 1M 上下文做长文档问答、代码库理解与长程检索
- 多语言：200+ 语言的理解、生成与翻译，或真实跨语言业务场景
- 端侧效率与硬件适配：4B/1.7B 量化（GGUF）、吞吐、TTFT/TPOT、显存/内存占用，NVIDIA / 昇腾 / 海光 / HOUMO.AI 等多硬件适配
- 指令遵循与推理：复杂指令、格式合规、数学与推理任务的真实评测
- 安全边界：高风险动作、越权工具调用、歧义检测、二次确认与安全拒绝
- 数据与训练：合法数据、难例挖掘、SFT/RL，用 LLaMA-Factory 微调并给出前后对比
- 前后对比：与更大模型、规则系统或其他同级开源模型在同一方法下对比

## 提交方式

1. Spark-X2.5 采用 Apache 2.0 许可，无需签署额外使用条款；使用时请遵守仓库 CODE_OF_CONDUCT 与 SECURITY 政策。
2. 安装并登录官方 HF CLI：

       pip install -U huggingface_hub
       hf auth login

3. 获取并记录固定 revision：

       hf download XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B --revision <commit-sha>

   国内可用 ModelScope / Modelers / SCNet / SourceFind 镜像，请注明来源与 revision。

4. 完成真实实验，保留可公开的运行日志、输入、原始输出、环境和截图。
5. 根据实际使用的模型，在对应的 Hugging Face Discussions 新建公开帖子：

   - Spark-X2.5-1.7B：https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B/discussions
   - Spark-X2.5-4B：https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B/discussions

   标题包含 `HER Hack-Astron #5` 即可，例如：

       [HER Hack-Astron #5] <案例名称>

6. 在本活动的 GitHub Issue 下回复你的 Discussion 直达链接，即完成提交。链接示例：

       https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B/discussions/<编号>
       https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B/discussions/<编号>

## 验收标准

全部满足才是有效案例：

1. **真实使用。** 提供完整 tested revision 和已脱敏的 snapshot/产物信息。
2. **真实运行。** 有代表性输入、原始 Spark-X2.5 输出，以及截图或日志证据。
3. **唯一发布渠道。** 完整案例发布在指定 Spark-X2.5 Discussion；GitHub-only 或其他平台-only 不接受。
4. **可复现。** 记录 runtime 版本（vLLM/SGLang/llama.cpp 及镜像 tag）、硬件、精度/量化、参数和必要脚本。
5. **指标诚实。** 准确率、延迟、显存或吞吐必须写样本量、方法、warm-up 和环境。
6. **包含边界。** 不只展示成功样例，也说明失败、限制或安全风险。
7. **原创与许可。** 使用自己的实验和文字；新增数据必须写明许可或授权。
8. **隐私与安全。** 不泄露 HF token、个人缓存路径、私有数据、内网地址或业务数据。
9. **不上传权重。** Discussion 和 GitHub Issue 回复中不要上传 safetensors、GGUF、PT、PTH 或 CKPT 权重文件；GGUF 请通过 HF/镜像发布，并仅附下载链接。

团队参赛时，请在 GitHub Issue 留言中列出所有参与贡献者，其中女性 Profile 贡献者占比须大于或等于 50%。

Nothing in the SDK accepts an `AbortSignal`. `pollForAttestation` (`src/iris/poll.ts:133-170`), `pollTransactionStatus` (`src/chains/stellar.ts:71-86`), and `waitForAllowance`/`retryOnTransientRpcLag` (`src/chains/stellar.ts:210-294`) all run `while` loops with fixed deadlines and no external cancellation. A service shutting down, a user navigating away from the demo, or a request-scoped timeout in a web backend cannot stop an in-flight transfer. This matters most after the burn: the README and `TransferError` docs promise the caller keeps `burnTxHash` for recovery, so an abort that discards it would violate the SDK's core safety contract.

**Proposed Change**
Thread an optional `signal?: AbortSignal` through `TransferOptionsBase` and `CompleteMintOptions`, honoring it in every polling/sleep loop (abortable sleep, not `setTimeout` fire-and-forget). Semantics: aborting before the burn throws a plain `AbortError` with nothing lost; aborting after the burn has been submitted throws a `TransferError` that still carries `burnTxHash` and sets `code` appropriately, so the recovery path is identical to any other post-burn failure. Fetches to Iris should pass the signal through.

- `transfer()` and `completeMint()` accept `options.signal` and the type surface compiles.
- Pre-burn abort rejects without submitting anything and without requiring recovery.
- Post-burn abort rejects with a `TransferError` whose `burnTxHash` is the real submitted hash.
- `pollForAttestation` aborts promptly (well before `pollTimeout`) and Iris `fetch` receives the signal.
- Tests cover pre-burn and post-burn abort with mocked chain calls.

## Description

Sensitive actions such as updating fee configuration (`src/app/api/fee-config/route.ts`), rotating organization master keys, or modifying RBAC role assignments rely solely on existing session cookies. If a user's browser is temporarily unattended, an attacker could perform high-impact admin mutations without wallet signature re-verification.

## Proposed Solution

1. Implement a "sudo mode" challenge middleware in `src/lib/session-sudo.ts`.
2. Require a fresh wallet challenge signature if the active session's last cryptographic verification was older than 15 minutes.
3. Return HTTP 403 `SUDO_REQUIRED` with a challenge payload when re-authentication is required.
4. Add frontend modal prompting quick Freighter re-signing before continuing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Critical admin operations require cryptographic wallet signature if session verification is older than 15m
- [ ] Non-critical read and standard operations proceed without interruption
- [ ] E2E security test in `e2e/admin-rbac.spec.ts` verifies re-auth enforcement

## Files to Modify
- src/lib/session-sudo.ts
- src/app/api/fee-config/route.ts
- src/app/api/rbac/route.ts
- e2e/admin-rbac.spec.ts

## 站点 1：`pathspecs` 的「白名单」按**目录**授予

`md_cg/sleep.py:311-327`（`pathspecs()` 返回**盘上非空的层目录名**）→ `:513` `_git_ok(..., "add", "--", *ps)`。

`git add -- <层名>` 会暂存该目录下**任何**未跟踪/已修改文件——于是层目录内的非 `.md` 件（运行态、原子写被杀留下的临时件、手工投放的任何文件）一并入册并提交进 `lib.git`。

引擎侧的既有口径与之相反：`fsutil.atomic_write` 的临时件是 `.<basename>.tmp-<rand>`（`fsutil.py:71` mkstemp 前缀），`sustain._list_stale_temps` 用 `.tmp-` 中缀识别它们；`sustain` 自己的 `_rebase`（#145 的参考补丁）用的是**文件 glob** `":(glob)<layer>/**/*.md"`，注释逐字「不含 .tmp/.lock 等」。

## 站点 2：§4.5 判据一的禁入后缀与真实命名**口径分叉**

`md_cg/sleep.py:84-85`：

```python
FORBIDDEN_BASENAMES = ("_keys.json", "_access.log", "_index.json")
FORBIDDEN_SUFFIXES = (".tmp", ".lock")
```

`:813-823` 用 `base.endswith(FORBIDDEN_SUFFIXES)` 判定。而仓内真实临时件名以 **`.tmp-<rand>`** 结尾（`.tmp` 是**中缀**）⇒ 同一份历史里老式 `junk.tmp` 被命中、`.n_a.md.tmp-k1lled` **漏报**，`audit_history['ok']=True`、`sleep --audit` 退出码 0。

**与站点 1 的关系**：入册前提来自站点 1；即使站点 1 按 `.md` 限定修掉，判据面对**经他途入册**的 `.tmp-` 件仍失明（两处各自独立成立）。`audit_tracking`（`:826-834`）只判 tracked 的**首个路径段**是否属 LAYERS，因此也看不见非 `.md` 件（读数见上）。

`pollForAttestation` in `src/iris/poll.ts:133-170` tolerates up to 5 consecutive failures before giving up — the right policy against a public API. But `getAttestation` (lines 102-122), used by `resolveBurn` in `src/transfer.ts:285-304`, calls `pollOnce` exactly once and throws `IrisRequestError` on the first failure. So `resolveBurn`, the SDK's read-only "what did this burn commit to?" helper, is strictly less reliable than the polling path for no documented reason. A single dropped connection makes a caller believe the burn is unresolvable.

**Proposed Change**
Give `getAttestation` the same consecutive-failure tolerance as `pollForAttestation` (extract the shared constant and a small retry helper so the policy lives in one place). `getAttestation` should still make exactly one *successful* read — it must not wait for indexing like the poll loop does; only transient failures retry.

**Acceptance Criteria**

- `getAttestation` retries on `IrisRequestError`-class failures up to the shared consecutive-failure limit and succeeds when a retry succeeds.
- `getAttestation` still throws `AttestationNotReadyError` on 404 / empty messages without retrying (404 is an expected state, not a failure).

`pollTransactionStatus` in `src/chains/stellar.ts:71-86` calls `server.getTransaction(hash)` inside a bare `while` loop with no error handling. A single transient RPC failure (connection reset, 5xx from the Soroban RPC) rejects the whole loop with whatever error the Stellar SDK threw — a bare error with no hash attached. This contradicts the module's own contract: the comment directly below (lines 81-85) says the hash must be surfaced via `SubmissionTimeoutError` because the transaction was already broadcast. Today that guarantee only holds for the timeout path, not the more common blip path. A caller that gets the bare error loses the only handle for recovering a possibly-landed transaction.

**Proposed Change**
Wrap `getTransaction` so transient failures increment a consecutive-failure counter and retry with a short backoff, mirroring the tolerance policy already used for Iris in `src/iris/poll.ts` (`IRIS_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES`). When the overall deadline passes — whether from repeated transient failures or simply never confirming — throw `SubmissionTimeoutError` carrying the hash. Genuinely terminal statuses (`FAILED`) keep throwing immediately.

**Acceptance Criteria**

- A mocked `getTransaction` that throws N-1 times transiently then returns `SUCCESS` resolves with the hash.
- A mocked `getTransaction` that always throws rejects with `SubmissionTimeoutError` whose `.hash` equals the submitted hash.
- `FAILED` status still rejects immediately without exhausting retries.
- Retry count and backoff are constants with a short comment explaining the tolerance, consistent with `src/iris/poll.ts`.
- Verified by the `typecheck-test-build` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## 一句话结论（快测能给的说法）

被测仓是 `FuRongJun-1999/lingshu` 的**完全重写版**（Liyang 线），一套 Python 记忆引擎，
**不是 DSH 插件**（全仓 grep `dsh-plugin|cordis|DSH_HOME` 在 `*.py` 与 `README.md` 上均 **0 命中**，
也没有 `dsh-plugin.json` / `cordis.patch.yml` / `.github/`），因此本件按**记忆域**体例走。

快测记录三句话：

1. **安装干净**：`uv venv` 3.12.13 + `uv pip install -e ".[full,dev]"` 一次过（9 包，RC=0）。
2. **自带 pytest 全量 2797 过 / 1 跳过 / 0 红**（129.54 s，RC=0），与 README §3 自报的 `2797 passed, 1 skipped` **逐项一致**；
   唯一那条 skip 是缺上游 `tests/` 目录时的**设计行为**，不是失败。
3. **作者自建的 `evalsuite` 能在第三方机器上原样复跑**（本次做到了），但要先设 `PYTHONUTF8=1`；
   复跑通后拿到本次最硬的一组对照：**同一份自建规则、同一台机器、同一个 N=1000 档**下，
   旧实现 `lingshu.core.core` 总分 **38.0**（探针 16.8 / 性质 67.4 / 性能 25.1 / 质量 48.8），
   新实现 `lingshu_ng.compat` 总分 **99.7**（探针 99.2 / 性质 100.0 / 性能 100.0 / 质量 100.0）。

**但这组分数不能当第三方能力结论**：规则版本（`RULES_VERSION = "evalsuite-rules-v1"`）、
四项权重（`probes 0.40 / props 0.30 / perf 0.15 / quality 0.15`）、131 条探针、15 条性质、
质量度量阈值**全部由被测方自己写定**，本机没有第三方任务集、也没有冻结的统计规范。
所以三张单里**「能力」记未测**，自建榜分数只作「同一口径下的改前 vs 改后相对读数」呈现。

`09d34f94a7d97fa6e38f9a478b2a9e39a4d8c74d`（`truncated=false`，505 entries / 471 blobs）比对：

### 4) 自建榜 `evalsuite` 第三方复跑（本次关键）

做法：在被测树**之外**做隔离副本，保证被测树不留产物。

```text
mkdir -p eval/ng-scratch
cp -r eval/lingshu_ng/{lingshu,lingshu_ng,evalsuite,tests_ng,pyproject.toml} eval/ng-scratch/   # 11M
```

**第一次原样跑：崩（RC=1）**

```text
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'splitlines'   @ evalsuite/common.py:43 (list_items)
  ... 子线程 traceback:
UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xa4 in position 71: illegal multibyte sequence
  @ subprocess.py:1599 _readerthread
```

根因：`evalsuite/common.py:23`（`run_child`）与 `:41`（`list_items`）两处
`subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, text=True)` **都没有写 `encoding=`**，
Windows 上按 **locale(GBK)** 解码，而子进程输出含 UTF-8 中文 → 解码失败 → `r.stdout` 为 `None` → `common.py:43` 抛 `AttributeError`。

补 `encoding` 还会撞第二处：`UnicodeEncodeError: 'gbk' codec can't encode character '\\u21c4' in position 21 @ run_all.py:451`
（`json.dump` 打开输出文件时同样按 locale 编码）。

**零改代码的解法：设 `PYTHONUTF8=1`。**

```text
cd eval/ng-scratch
PYTHONUTF8=1 <venv python> evalsuite/run_all.py --snap ng=. --skip legacy --sizes 1000 --perf-rounds 1 --workers 4 \
    --out out/ng_run.json --md out/ng_run.md
# RC=0 ｜ 探针=131 性质=15 workers=4
# probes 67s → props 128s → legacy 附表 128s → perf ng N=1000 round0 ERR 0.012s → 完成 131s
# ng 总分 84.7 | 探针 99.2 性质 100.0 性能 0.0 质量 100.0
```

- 探针 **131 条，只有 1 条非 OK**：`i176-time-based`（`0.02s 墙钟内 50 次 decay 后 importance 0.5→0.182`）——
  正是作者在 `LEADERBOARD_NG.md` 自述的那条「遗忘按调用次数计，而不是按墙钟」。
- 性质 **15 条全 OK（非 OK = 0）**。
- 质量：`{available:true, scope:"lingshu_ng", modules:113, total_lines:20614, total_sloc:16925, max_module:{module:"lingshu_ng\\world\\compat.py", lines:752, sloc:601}}`
  （其后 `nn/net.py` 507 / `world/world_model.py` 503）。

**结论：修法只是设一个环境变量，不改被测方任何一行代码；但必须知道要设**——否则在 zh-CN Windows 上照 README 快速开始跑自建榜会直接崩。
这是**可复跑性摩擦（测试侧缺口）**，不是被测引擎的缺陷。

## 红项与归因逐条（每条都追到源码行）

### A) `evalsuite/common.py:23/:41` 缺 `encoding` → zh-CN Windows 上崩 —— **测试侧缺口，不是被测引擎缺陷**

- 行号：`common.py:23`（`run_child`）、`common.py:41`（`list_items`）、崩点 `common.py:43`；第二处 `run_all.py:451`。
- 触发：`subprocess.run(..., text=True)` 在 Windows 上按 locale(GBK) 解码含 UTF-8 中文的子进程输出。
- 解法：`PYTHONUTF8=1`（零改代码，本次实测 RC=0）。
- 定性：**可复跑性摩擦**，属测评工具链问题，**不计入被测产品质量**。

### B) `evalsuite/perf.py:14` `import resource` → Windows 上 perf 整格 ERR，0.15 权重直接丢 —— **平台不兼容，属测试侧缺口**

- `evalsuite/perf.py` 共 83 行，只有两处用到 `resource`：
  第 **14 行** `import resource`；第 **82 行** `out["maxrss_mb"] = round(resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / 1024, 1)`。
- `resource` 是 **Unix-only** 标准库模块 → Windows 上 perf 子进程在 import 阶段就死。
- 原始读数：`perf.ng.1000 = {"verdict":"ERR","reading":"ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'resource' @ File …\\evalsuite\\perf.py, line 14, in <module>","sec":0.012}`。
- `run_perf` 的策略是**非 OK 直接 break**，所以一格 ERR 就把整个 perf 维度判零。
- **补桩对照（确认 resource 是唯一阻塞点）**：`eval/ng-shim/resource.py` 提供 `RUSAGE_SELF=0` / `RUSAGE_CHILDREN=-1` /
  `class _Usage`（`ru_maxrss=0`）/ `def getrusage(who=0)`，以 `PYTHONPATH=<ng-scratch>;<ng-shim>;<ng-scratch>/evalsuite` 跑
  `probe_runner.py --impl ng --perf 1000`：

```text
`RESULT {"n": 1000, "build_s": 3.33, "first_read_ms": 115.7, "add": 6.965, "recall": 8.844,
           "decay_cycle": 5.507, "self_check": 0.056, "activation": 4.527,
           "maxrss_mb": 0.0, "verdict": "OK", "sec": 5.073}
```

  即 `verdict` 由 `ERR` 转 `OK`，五档操作读数全部拿到 → **resource 是唯一阻塞点**。

> 工具坑：`probe_runner.py --perf` 的 `PYTHONPATH` 必须是 **Windows 分号形式**（`D:/…;D:/…`）；
> MSYS 的 `/cygdrive/...` 冒号形式**静默不生效**，仍报 `No module named 'resource'`。

见上 §3。发布包不含上游 `tests/`，检查优雅跳过；把上游 `tests/` 放到仓库根即可启用。

- `lingshu/world/voxel_world.py:95`：`self.size = min(int(size), self.MAX_SIZE)  # 区块边长（钳到 MAX_SIZE）`
- `lingshu/world/voxel_world.py:105`：`def build_flatland(self, trees: int = 2, water: bool = True) -> int:`
- `lingshu/core/core.py:7394`（门面 docstring）：`- build: 生成平地世界（params: size, trees, water）`
- `lingshu/core/core.py:7411`：`blocks = self._voxel.build_flatland(trees=int(p.get("trees", 2)), water=bool(p.get("water", True)))`

docstring 列的三条上界与实现**一致**（下面「对照实测」A1/A2/A3 逐条验到）——本件不是「文档说 A、代码做 B」。
本件主张的是一处**未被这三条覆盖的调用方可控循环次数**：`trees`。

## 机制 / 根因

1. `build_flatland`（`voxel_world.py:105-134`）的循环次数 = 入参 `trees`：`:119` `for _ in range(trees):`，循环体内每棵树写 12 个 dict 条目并 `count += 12`。函数内**没有**对 `trees` 的比较（语句级读数见证据表 E3 行）。
2. 同一措施覆盖的另外三处都在钳：`size` 在 `__init__:95`、`steps` 在 `simulate:171`、轨迹长度在 `_record_trail:192-193`。
3. 门面 `core.py:7411` 从动作参数取 `trees`，`int()` 之后直接进调用——门面层不放闸（E3）。
4. 后果的形状：`blocks` 的键受 `(tx, tz) ∈ [2, size-3]²` 限制，所以**字典大小有上界**（实测 1140）；`count` 是普通整数累加，`range(trees)` 的迭代次数才是随入参线性增长的那一项。因此可观测后果是**单次调用占满 CPU 的时间**，不是分配量。
5. 入径面**至少 8 条**：除门面 `voxel_world("build")`（`core.py:7411`）外，`core.py` 还有 7 处
   `create_scene(trees=int(p.get("trees", …)))`（`:7577/:7681/:7745/:7822/:7910/:8345/:8433`），
   而 `SceneSimulator.create_scene`（`scene_simulator.py:142`）同样把 `trees` 原样交给 `build_flatland`；
   这 8 条实测在 `trees=200000` 下全部 `status=ok`（实测 5）。⇒ **把上界加在 `VoxelWorld` 层是一处覆盖 8 条；
   加在门面层则要逐门面各加一次**（这是修法层面的推论，本件不主张具体取态）。

the real limit is never named

**Source:** Q1 human user-testing round 1 (2026-10-13 PDT), H-J6 error-copy journey, live against https://room.trydemigod.com in a sandbox room. Log: `~/workspace/bug-hunt/qa-live/human-round1-log.md` §H-J6.6.

### Exact failing step (live, reproduced)
1. As a room member, `POST /api/rooms/q1-human-r1-x7/files` staging a 1,050,000-byte file (room attachment cap is 1,048,576 bytes) as canonical base64 (`data` = 1,400,000 chars; total JSON body 1,400,099 bytes, under the route body limit).
2. Response: HTTP 422 `invalid_attachment` — `"data must be canonical base64 with no whitespace"`.

The data **was** canonical base64. The file was simply over the size cap. The response never states the cap (1 MiB) or the actual size, and the implied remedy (fix your encoding) is wrong.

### Mechanism (source)
`server/room-attachment-bytes.mjs`: `validAttachmentData()` returns `false` when the base64 string length exceeds `base64LengthForBytes(attachmentLimits.fileBytes)`, folding the size violation into the encoding check; `decodeData()` then reports the encoding error. The correct branch — HTTP 413 `attachment_too_large`, "File exceeds the room attachment size limit" (`bytes.length > fileBytes`) — is **unreachable** for base64 input, because any over-cap byte string necessarily has an over-cap base64 length and fails one check earlier.

### Sibling instance (same pattern, JSON routes)
A 20,116-byte **valid** JSON body to `POST /api/rooms/<room>/bounties` returns HTTP 422 `invalid_bounty_input`, `"Expected a JSON body."` — again the wrong reason: the body exceeded the 16,384-byte JSON limit. The accurate 413 copy exists in `server/http.mjs` ("Request body is N bytes; the limit is 16384 bytes") but the escrow routes' catch-all body reader (`readPayload` in `server/bounty-escrow-routes.mjs`) swallows it. Verified with a direct single-encoded curl and a small-body sanity post (201).

### Controls (same run)
- An 8-byte text file stages fine (201, `state: staged`).
- A `.exe` upload is refused with clear copy (422 `blocked_extension`: 'extension ".exe" is blocked for security').

### Expected
Oversize refusals say so: name the limit and the actual size (e.g. the existing 413 `attachment_too_large` / `too_large` shapes), on both the file-staging route and the JSON body path.

Cross-refs: error-registry family #3365 (copy quality, not code migration). QA logs failures only; no product code changed.

## Goal
Provide one clear private route for external vulnerability reports and one reproducible internal process to receive, triage, remediate, retest and close security findings without exposing exploit details, credentials, customer data or sensitive infrastructure information in public issues.

## External disclosure contract
- Publish/maintain a consistent `SECURITY.md` or equivalent entry point for each public/relevant repository.
- Direct reporters to GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting when enabled/appropriate, otherwise to an approved private channel.
- Explicitly prohibit sensitive exploit details, credentials and customer data in public issues/PRs.
- State supported/current release scope sufficiently to route reports without making unsupported SLA/legal promises.
- Avoid promising bounty/payment unless a separate program explicitly exists.

## Internal response lifecycle
`private intake → validate/reproduce → severity/business impact → owner → containment if needed → remediation PR → regression/adversarial test → security/CI gates → independent retest where warranted → coordinated closure/disclosure decision`

Required controls:
- deduplicate related reports without losing provenance;
- preserve minimized evidence and affected release/commit;
- apply existing Critical/High release-blocking rules;
- distinguish unconfirmed reports from verified vulnerabilities;
- record remediation/retest evidence;
- feed confirmed root causes into the continuous-improvement/debt process (#299);
- never close a finding solely because a scanner no longer reports it without validating the actual vulnerability path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Product-wide disclosure policy and private intake route are documented.
- [x] Relevant repositories link to one consistent process without conflicting instructions.
- [x] Triage fields include affected surface/version, severity, exploitability/impact, Tenant/security boundary relevance, owner and state.
- [x] Critical/High confirmed repository-controlled findings block release under existing policy.
- [x] Remediation requires regression/adversarial coverage where feasible and exact-head security/CI evidence.
- [x] Retest/closure criteria are documented, including when independent retest is required.
- [x] Root-cause/process improvements flow into #299 / SSDF continuous improvement.
- [x] No sensitive vulnerability details are copied into public roadmap issues as part of normal triage.
- [x] The process is tested with one synthetic/private dry-run without creating a real exploitable vulnerability.

## Non-goals
- Creating a paid bug bounty.
- Publishing exploit proof-of-concepts.
- Promising response/remediation SLAs that operations cannot support.

References:
- NIST SP 800-216: https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/216/final
- NIST SSDF: https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/ssdf

## CRA relationship

This issue owns the technical/private vulnerability intake, triage, remediation and retest capability. It does not decide whether Conference Manager is legally in scope of the EU Cyber Resilience Act or submit regulatory notifications. SaaS 7 #305 owns CRA applicability and, if applicable, the Single Reporting Platform/24h/72h/final-report operating process. Confirmed CRA-relevant findings must be transferable from this private response workflow into that regulatory process without publishing sensitive exploit details.

**Context**
`src/lib/chain/decimal.ts:81-88` — `toAtomic` parses with `DECIMAL_RE` but on a
regex miss (`:84`) falls back to `parseDecimalFromFloat` (`:91-94`):
`BigInt(Math.round(value * 10 ** decimals))`. For JSON-number inputs this
reintroduces exactly the floating-point error the module exists to avoid —
values beyond 2^53 scaled lose precision at the wei/stroop boundary, and
`Math.round` can shift an amount by one atomic unit. Callers include balance
math in `stellar.ts:140`.

**Proposed Change**
Either reject non-string inputs with a typed error (check call sites first), or
convert number inputs exactly via `toString()` + `DECIMAL_RE` — never
`value * 10 ** decimals`. Valid string inputs must behave identically.

**Acceptance Criteria**

- No `Math.round(value * 10 ** decimals)` path remains.
- Existing `tests/decimal.test.ts` stays green (no behavioral change for valid
  strings).
- New tests: float-boundary inputs (`0.1`, `1e-7`, large amounts) yield exact
  `BigInt` results or explicit errors — never a silently rounded value.
- Verified by `npm test`.

Forgetting an Apple Watch from Settings disconnects and disposes the `WatchTransport`, which only cancels timers and closes Dart streams. It never sends `stopRecording()` to the Watch, so the Watch keeps recording after the phone says the device is forgotten, and the phone no longer consumes that audio. Reproduced on the iOS Simulator with the real `DeviceService`, `AppleWatchDeviceConnection` and `WatchTransport`.

**Product impact** (see [PRODUCT.md](https://github.com/BasedHardware/Omi/blob/main/PRODUCT.md) and [ISSUE_TRIAGE_GUIDE.MD](https://github.com/BasedHardware/Omi/blob/main/ISSUE_TRIAGE_GUIDE.MD))

- Primary loop layer: Capture
- [x] Involves data loss, failed capture, or broken sync/trust. Broken trust: the microphone keeps running after an explicit "forget".

**Describe the bug**

`WatchTransport` has a `stopRecording()` method that does stop the Watch engine; neither `disconnect()` nor `dispose()` calls it.

**To Reproduce**

1. Pair an Apple Watch and start recording from it.
2. Phone: Settings → Device → **Forget Device** → confirm.
3. The Watch still shows recording; its mic stays on.

**Current behavior**

Zero `stopRecording` calls; the Watch stays in recording state.

**Expected behavior**

Disconnecting or forgetting a Watch stops its recorder first (best effort), then closes the transport.

**Screenshots**

No screenshot (no Watch on the Simulator). Evidence below.

**user ID (can we access the user info to validate the bug?):**

Not needed: found in the code and reproduced without a user account (local fixture backend).

**Smartphone + device (please complete the following information):**

- Device: iOS Simulator, iPhone 16 (reproduction); the bug is in shared code, so physical iPhones are affected too
- OS: iOS 18.0 (Simulator)
- App Version: `main` at cf8201c2f5 (dev flavor)
- Device version: Apple Watch (omiWatchApp)

**Additional context**

*Root cause.* [Forget Device](https://github.com/BasedHardware/omi/blob/cf8201c2f532bacb24dfcd4f19412cf26b386e47/app/lib/pages/settings/device_settings.dart#L339) goes through `DeviceService`; [`AppleWatchDeviceConnection`](https://github.com/BasedHardware/omi/blob/cf8201c2f532bacb24dfcd4f19412cf26b386e47/app/lib/services/devices/connectors/apple_watch_connection.dart#L123) delegates disconnect to the transport. [`WatchTransport.disconnect`](https://github.com/BasedHardware/omi/blob/cf8201c2f532bacb24dfcd4f19412cf26b386e47/app/lib/services/devices/transports/watch_transport.dart#L122-L140) and [`dispose`](https://github.com/BasedHardware/omi/blob/cf8201c2f532bacb24dfcd4f19412cf26b386e47/app/lib/services/devices/transports/watch_transport.dart#L307-L315) cancel timers and close streams but never call [`stopRecording()`](https://github.com/BasedHardware/omi/blob/cf8201c2f532bacb24dfcd4f19412cf26b386e47/app/lib/services/devices/transports/watch_transport.dart#L269-L273), the only path that reaches `WatchAudioRecorderViewModel.stopRecording` on the Watch.

*Reproduction.* Reproduced on the iOS Simulator (iPhone 16, iOS 18.0) with a temporary integration test on `main` at `cf8201c2f5`. The test drives the real production classes; only the platform boundary is faked (the `WatchRecorderHostAPI` pigeon, tracking start/stop calls). Start recording, then `DeviceService.forgetDevice`:

Neither is true today, so the desktop Swift suite is red on main (first seen on PR #11479's CI; reproduced at main `8442e89f03`), which also blocks the hourly desktop release train's qualification lane.

Facts:
- `TaskAssistantSettings.defaultAnalysisPrompt` is ~13.7k chars, and has been over 10k since at least 2026-06 (14.3k on Jul 1). It has therefore never synced: `SettingsSyncManager.promptForSync` deliberately omits oversized prompts to keep partial PATCH semantics.
- Backend `ASSISTANT_ANALYSIS_PROMPT_MAX_LENGTH = 10000` (`backend/routers/users.py`, task model), same 10k as insight/memory; the client's `TaskAssistantSettings.maximumSyncedAnalysisPromptLength` is also 10_000.

Raising the bound is NOT client-safe on its own: if the client constant is raised before the backend limit is deployed to prod, every user on the default task prompt starts including a ~13.7k `analysis_prompt` in the settings PATCH, Pydantic 422s, and the entire assistant-settings sync breaks for that build. Sequence must be: raise backend limit → deploy prod backend → then raise the client constant in a desktop release.

PR #11479 restores the two tests to assert the shipped contract (oversized default is omitted; all three assistants share the 10k bound) so main and the release train are unblocked; this issue tracks Problem
Documentation and help articles contain outdated/incorrect info about device hardware behavior after recent firmware updates.

## What needs updating

### 1. LED charging colors (URGENT)
**Outdated:** Some docs mention "orange" LED during charging

**Current (correct):**
- Alternating green/blue OR green/red = charging
- Solid green = fully charged
- Red = disconnected (not charging-related)
- Blue = connected
- No light = device off

### 2. Power on/off instructions
Need clear step-by-step for:
- Turning device on (first boot + regular)
- Turning device off
- Restart/reset

### 3. Tap & Talk usage
Document how Tap & Talk works:
- How to trigger it
- What it does
- Difference vs normal recording

## Where to update
- Help center articles (help.omi.me or equivalent)
- docs.omi.me hardware section
- Quick start guide / user manual
- In-app help text (if applicable)

## Impact
Users reporting confusion about charging LEDs due to outdated docs → support tickets + frustration.

Tasks only show up in the home screen widget on the day they're due. Nothing appears ahead of time, even for tasks that need real lead time.

Request:

The task widget should show what's due today AND flag upcoming tasks that are time-intensive or high-priority. Ideally users could set a lookahead window, something like the next 3 days OR if we could flag tasks as high priority, so things don't just appear the day of.

Note:

This is tied to my request for separate toggles (Goal Tracking, Daily Score, and Tasks on Home Screen).

impact**
- Primary loop layer: Python CLI (`omi auth login --browser`, `omi chat`).
- `omi chat` cannot be reached through any supported login. Every invocation exits 1 with "Chat requires browser sign-in" and tells the user to run `omi auth login --browser`, which is exactly the command that produces the rejected profile. The whole chat command is dead for real users.

**Describe the bug**
On main `8ece568b16`:
- `omi_cli/auth/oauth.py` `login_with_browser` signs into Firebase, mints a developer API key from that session and returns `store_api_key(...)`, which sets `auth_method = "api_key"` and nulls `id_token` / `refresh_token` (since "browser OAuth mints a dev API key", e9368db636).
- `omi_cli/commands/chat.py` (added later in #20685) gates on `profile.auth_method != "oauth"` and raises the usage error above.
- The only way to use chat is to hand-write an `auth_method = "oauth"` profile with Firebase tokens in `config.toml`, which is what `tests/test_chat.py::_oauth_profile` does via `store_oauth_tokens`, so the suite never exercises the real login path.

**To reproduce (offline, synthetic data)**
Run `omi --json auth login --browser` end to end with respx mocks for `/v1/auth/token`, identitytoolkit, `/v1/dev/keys` and `/v1/dev/key`, and a fake `webbrowser.open` that hits the loopback callback with the right `state`:
```
login payload: {'profile': 'default', 'auth_method': 'api_key', ...}
stored auth_method: api_key   id_token: None   refresh_token: None
omi --json chat --history  ->  exit 1, {"error": "Chat requires browser sign-in", "detail": "Run `omi auth login --browser`, then try `omi chat` again. ..."}
```
`/v2/messages` is never called.

**Expected behavior**
After `omi auth login --browser`, `omi chat` works. `/v1/dev/*` commands keep using the minted developer key; `/v2/messages` uses the signed-in user's Firebase ID token, refreshed from the refresh token when it expires.

**Fix**
Browser sign-in keeps the Firebase session (`id_token`, `refresh_token`, expiry) on the `api_key` profile beside the key (the `Profile` fields already exist). `OmiClient` gains an explicit `firebase_session` seam that authenticates with the ID token and refreshes it in place without touching the key or the auth method; `omi chat` uses that seam and gates on the presence of a session instead of the `oauth` label. A pasted key (`omi auth login --api-key`) still drops any session. Legacy `oauth` profiles keep working. Regression tests run the real login command against mocked providers and then `omi chat` on the profile it wrote. PR follows.

Two defects in `src/components/Browse.tsx`:

- Verified by `npm test` plus a keyboard/screen-reader spot check.

The smallest `.hy` program that demonstrates it

```hy
// nested-call.hy
fn same(s []int) []int { return s }

fn worker(s []int) {
    for i in 0..200000 { s[0] = i }
}

fn main() {
    s := []int{1, 2, 3}
    t := same(same(s))      // returns an alias of `s`, two call levels deep
    task worker(move t)     // spawn site: classified as a fresh call result
    for i in 0..200000 { s[0] = i }
}
```

* `hyb check nested-call.hy` → `OK (0 diagnostics)` (exit 0)
* main @ `f99d6d0b37722de206015be9e1c59b04e827c794`, built from that commit with rustc 1.99.0 / go1.26.9
* `hyb build --emit-go` → `go run -race` → **`WARNING: DATA RACE`**, `Found 1 data race(s)`, `exit status 66`

### What the checker should say

`HYB-E3003: write through a live alias of a moved value` at the trailing `s[0] = i` — exactly what it already says for the **one-level** form:

```hy
fn same(s []int) []int { return s }
fn main() {
    s := []int{1, 2, 3}
    t := same(s)
    task worker(move t)
    s[0] = 7          // HYB-E3003: write through a live alias of a moved value  ← already rejected
}
```

### What it actually said

`OK (0 diagnostics)`, and the emitted Go is:

```go
func main() {
	s := []int{1, 2, 3}
	t := same(same(s))
	go worker(t)              // same backing array as s
	for i := 0; i < 200000; i++ {
		s[0] = i              // concurrent write, no synchronization
	}
}
```

```
WARNING: DATA RACE
Write at 0x00c00001e090 by goroutine 7:
  main.worker()
Previous write at 0x00c00001e090 by main goroutine:
  main.main()
Found 1 data race(s)
exit status 66
```

### Six wrapper forms, all accepted, all racing

The edge is lost whenever the reference-typed value reaches the binding through anything other than a bare identifier (or a call whose argument is a bare identifier). Every row below is `hyb check` → `OK (0 diagnostics)` **and** `go run -race` → `WARNING: DATA RACE`:

| # | Shape | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `t := same(same(s))` | nested call |
| 2 | `t := same(s)[0:2]` | view of a call result |
| 3 | `w := wrap{items: same(s)}` / `u := b.items` | composite literal element |
| 4 | `t := box{items: s}.items` | field extracted from a literal |
| 5 | `t := take(box{items: s})` with `fn take(b box) []int { return b.items }` | call returning a parameter's field |
| 6 | `var t []int; for i in 0..1 { t = same(s) }` | **assignment** form (never records an alias) |

Negative controls that already reject correctly (so this is a gap, not the absence of the mechanism): `t := same(s)` (E3003), `t := s` (E3003), `t := s[:]` (E3003), `t := box{items: s}` (E3003), `task worker(same(m))` (E3001), `ch <- same(s)` (E3002).

### Why it is a bug, not a design choice

GUARANTEES rows 1 and 6: values crossing a `task` spawn are verified sendable, and a moved value cannot be used by the sender afterwards (O5.2). Here the sender keeps writing the same backing array the spawned task writes: a real write/write data race with zero diagnostics. It is not a `managed` region, not a Go-API escape, and not foreign code — it is the plain checked subset the claim covers.

### Root cause

`record_alias` in `compiler/crates/hy-check/src/loans.rs:577` records the O5.2 edge only for:

* `Expr::Ident { .. }` — a bare binding reference, and
* `Expr::Call { args, .. }` where some argument's `root_ident()` is `Some` — i.e. a **bare identifier argument**.

Everything else falls through `_ => {}`: a `Call` argument that is itself a call (1), an `Index`/`Slice` value (2), a `StructLit` value (3), a `Field` value (4), a `Call` whose argument is a `StructLit` (5). Separately, the assignment path (`process_assign` / `record_assign_borrow_aliases`) only handles `&x` borrows — a call result assigned to an existing binding (6) never calls `record_alias` at all.

### Fix

I am opening a PR that generalizes the alias collection to walk every reference-carrying sub-expression of the value (strip parens; descend through call arguments, composite-literal elements, and the base of field/index/slice expressions), recording an edge for every root binding found, and runs the same recording on the assignment path. Regression tests pin the six positive shapes above plus the five negative controls, so the widening cannot silently swallow the existing rejects.

### Context

* Rule: O5.2 freeze / A1b alias tracking; SPEC-LANGUAGE §9.3.
* Sibling to #38 / #73 / #74 (call-result laundering). The one-level fix from #74 works; this report is the wrapper tail that still walks past it.
* Platform: Windows host, checker built and run inside WSL Ubuntu (rustc 1.99.0, go1.26.9), `go run -race` for the race evidence.

### Minimal correction

The existing Deepgram client bounds its terminal send. Use the existing Parakeet drain timeout, including the same five-second fallback for zero, for this send as well:

```diff
-                    await ws.send("finalize")
+                    await asyncio.wait_for(
```

### Regression test

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from unittest.mock import patch

import pytest

from omi.stt.parakeet import ParakeetTranscriber


def test_cancellation_bounds_a_blocked_finalize_send_and_joins_receiver():
    async def scenario():
        receiving = asyncio.Event()
        finalizing = asyncio.Event()
        send_cancelled = asyncio.Event()
        receiver_cancelled = asyncio.Event()

        class BlockedWebSocket:
            closed = False

            async def __aenter__(self):
                return self

            async def __aexit__(self, *_):
                self.closed = True

            async def recv(self):
                return '{"type": "ready"}'

            async def send(self, chunk):
                assert chunk == "finalize"
                finalizing.set()
                try:
                    await asyncio.Event().wait()
                finally:
                    send_cancelled.set()

            def __aiter__(self):
                return self

            async def __anext__(self):
                receiving.set()
                try:
                    await asyncio.Event().wait()
                finally:
                    receiver_cancelled.set()

        ws = BlockedWebSocket()
        with patch("websockets.connect", return_value=ws):
            transcriber = ParakeetTranscriber(
                "https://fixture.invalid", drain_timeout=0.01
            )
            task = asyncio.create_task(transcriber.run(asyncio.Queue()))
            await asyncio.wait_for(receiving.wait(), timeout=1)
            task.cancel()
            await asyncio.wait_for(finalizing.wait(), timeout=1)
            with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
                await asyncio.wait_for(task, timeout=0.5)

        assert send_cancelled.is_set()
        assert receiver_cancelled.is_set()
        assert ws.closed
        assert asyncio.all_tasks() == {asyncio.current_task()}

    asyncio.run(scenario())
```

`pollTransactionStatus` in `src/chains/stellar.ts:71-86` calls `server.getTransaction(hash)` inside a bare `while` loop with no error handling. A single transient RPC failure (connection reset, 5xx from the Soroban RPC) rejects the whole loop with whatever error the Stellar SDK threw — a bare error with no hash attached. This contradicts the module's own contract: the comment directly below (lines 81-85) says the hash must be surfaced via `SubmissionTimeoutError` because the transaction was already broadcast. Today that guarantee only holds for the timeout path, not the more common blip path. A caller that gets the bare error loses the only handle for recovering a possibly-landed transaction.

**Proposed Change**
Wrap `getTransaction` so transient failures increment a consecutive-failure counter and retry with a short backoff, mirroring the tolerance policy already used for Iris in `src/iris/poll.ts` (`IRIS_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES`). When the overall deadline passes — whether from repeated transient failures or simply never confirming — throw `SubmissionTimeoutError` carrying the hash. Genuinely terminal statuses (`FAILED`) keep throwing immediately.

**Acceptance Criteria**

- A mocked `getTransaction` that throws N-1 times transiently then returns `SUCCESS` resolves with the hash.
- A mocked `getTransaction` that always throws rejects with `SubmissionTimeoutError` whose `.hash` equals the submitted hash.
- `FAILED` status still rejects immediately without exhausting retries.
- Retry count and backoff are constants with a short comment explaining the tolerance, consistent with `src/iris/poll.ts`.
- Verified by the `typecheck-test-build` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

for the maintainer on the combat redesign: PRD #259, with #256 (declaration), #257 (place of impact) and #258 (boarding). Each has a recommended default. Reply with a number and "yes" to take the default, or give your answer. Once these are settled, #259 is split into agent-ready slices.

## Captains and ships

1. **Pirate status after a captain dies.** Does the new captain start clean, or does the record (`G.pirates`, kept per player today) stay with the player?
   *Default: the new captain starts clean. The pirate was the captain, not the player. Bounties already paid stay paid.*
2. **Taking a ship.** When the winner takes the loser's ship, what happens to the winner's own ship?
   *Default: the winner moves across to the taken ship (crew, cargo and gold go with them), and the old ship is left adrift as floating loot. One ship per player stays the rule.*
3. **A taken ship's damage.** Does it keep its damage?
   *Default: yes, it keeps hull, mast and cannon damage. It sails home to be repaired.*
4. **Waiting for a new captain.** Does the player whose ship was lost miss anything before picking a new captain?
   *Default: they pick at the start of their next turn, then sail that turn from their home port.*

## Boarding

5. **Glory for boarding.** You didn't pick glory as a spoil. So does a boarding win give no glory, unlike sinking?
   *Default: the same glory as sinking when the ship is taken, and none when it's left.*
6. **Surrender.** Can a side give up partway through a crew fight?
   *Default: no. A crew fight is fought to the end.*
7. **Both crews reach 0 in the same round.**
   *Default: the boarding fails, both ships are left derelict, and both captains live.*
8. **Specialists** (gunner, navigator, surgeon …). They don't exist yet. Should they be designed now as their own PRD, or parked?
   *Default: park them. #258 ships without "take specialists", and the specialists design gets its own issue later.*

## Orders and the matchup (#259)

9. **Does the attacker get anything for declaring?**
   *Default: no. Choosing when and where to fight is the attacker's edge.*
10. **After an escape or a break-off,** does the fleeing ship (or, in a break-off, the defender) move one hex away, so the same two ships can't fight again that turn?
    *Default: yes.*
11. **How many rounds can a fight last?** Two Broadsides can trade fire round after round.
    *Default: no cap. The fight ends when a ship sinks, flees, breaks off or is boarded.*
12. **The balance numbers:** the weather gauge gives +1, fleeing into smoke gives +2, and boarding through smoke needs 4+.
    *Default: keep them as first guesses, to tune in play.*
13. **Wind direction in the rules.** The weather gauge needs the game logic to know the wind. Today it's pinned to one trade wind (`TRADE_WIND`). Should the wind ever change during a game? This matters for the event deck (#240) and the hurricane (#241).
    *Default: one fixed wind for now. If the wind changes later, it's stored in `G` and driven by events.*

## Place of impact (#257)

14. **The aimed tables:** Fire high is 1–2 Mast, 3–4 Crew, 5 Cannons, 6 Hull. Fire low is 1–3 Hull, 4–5 Cargo, 6 Cannons. Are you happy with these?
    *Default: yes.*
15. **Mast hits:** should enough of them dismast a ship (it can't flee until repaired), rather than having moves just stop at 1?
    *Default: no. Moves stop at 1, and further mast hits go to the hull, as #257 says.*

## Animation

16. **Who reads the reveal?** Should the order reveal play in full for every seat, or skip quickly for seats that aren't in the fight?
    *Default: in full for everyone, which is the social moment, with a skip button for bystanders.*

Sequence must be: raise backend limit → deploy prod backend → then raise the client constant in a desktop release.

PR #11479 restores the two tests to assert the shipped contract (oversized default is omitted; all three assistants share the 10k bound) so main and the release train are unblocked; this issue tracks add a light mode version of the app. Dark mode hurts my eyes.

Research published in the journal Ergonomics shows that the human visual system processes dark text on light backgrounds about 26% faster than light text on dark backgrounds.

This happens because the iris slightly constricts when viewing bright backgrounds, creating a smaller aperture that increases depth of field and sharpens focus on individual characters.

In contrast, dark mode keeps the pupil more dilated for longer periods. That reduces visual acuity and can make rapid text scanning harder, especially when users need to quickly locate specific information.

Studies from the Nielsen Norman Group also show that while dark mode can reduce eye strain in low-light environments, light mode is generally better for sustained reading and quick information retrieval.

Because of this, offering a light mode option would greatly improve accessibility and usability for many users.

This would be amazing. 🙏

(`src/bounties/bounties.service.ts:119-166`) still has the exact bug described by (closed) issue #102 ("BountiesService.markMergedAndRelease marks a team-assigned bounty PAID even when team.splits is empty, skipping the payout entirely"):
```ts
if (bounty.teamId) {
  const team = await this.teamRepo.findOne({
    where: { id: bounty.teamId },
    relations: { splits: true },
  });
  if (team && team.splits.length > 0) {
    ...
    await this.escrowService.splitRelease(bounty.escrowId, recipients);
  }
} else if (bounty.claimedById) {
  ...
  await this.escrowService.release(bounty.escrowId, contributor?.stellarAddress ?? '', bounty.claimedById);
}

assertTransition(bounty.status, BountyStatus.PAID);
bounty.status = BountyStatus.PAID;
bounty.paidAt = new Date();
const paid = await this.bountyRepo.save(bounty);
```
When `bounty.teamId` is set but the team's `splits` array is empty (`team.splits.length === 0`) — a real, reachable state: `TeamsService.create` doesn't require at least one split at creation for a team that's later assigned via `assignToBounty`, and `TeamsService.updateSplits` can be called to clear a team's splits after assignment — neither the `if (team && team.splits.length > 0)` branch nor the `else if (bounty.claimedById)` branch executes (it's an `if`/`else if`, and the outer `if (bounty.teamId)` already consumed the branch regardless of whether the inner `team.splits.length > 0` check passed). No `escrowService.release`/`splitRelease` call happens at all. Execution falls straight through to `assertTransition(bounty.status, BountyStatus.PAID)` and the bounty is unconditionally marked `PAID`, `paidAt` is set, and the function returns success — with the sponsor's escrowed funds still fully `LOCKED` on-chain, no `Payment` row ever created, and no error surfaced to any caller (the webhook handler, the bounty record, and any dashboard all show a normal-looking completed, paid bounty).

Tracing the closing PR: `gh issue view 102 --json closedByPullRequestsReferences` points to PR #207. `gh pr view 207` shows its title is "fix: gate Swagger in production, stop deposit clobbering monthlyDeposit, raise stale idempotency window" and its changed files are `src/common/idempotency/idempotency.interceptor.ts(.spec.ts)`, `src/main.ts`, `src/maintenance-pool/dto/create-pool.dto.ts`, `src/maintenance-pool/maintenance-pool.service.(spec.)ts` — its body batch-closes `Closes #90\nCloses #93\nCloses #99\nCloses #102`, and it does legitimately fix #90/#93/#99, but `src/bounties/bounties.service.ts` is never touched, so #102 was closed without any corresponding fix. This is the same "closed by a partially-unrelated batch-closing PR" pattern already found for #1, #10, #25, #48, #56, #120, #126, and #127 elsewhere in this repo's history.

**Fix**: when `bounty.teamId` is set but the resolved team has no splits (or the team itself can't be found), either fall back to releasing to `bounty.claimedById` directly (if set), or throw an explicit error instead of silently proceeding to `PAID` with no release — a team-assigned bounty with zero configured splits should block the merge-to-paid transition with a clear "team has no payout splits configured" error, not silently swallow the payout.

I checked the UAE Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs & Port Security sources current in 2026. On 25 June 2026 the UAE expanded the "nationals of certain countries residing abroad" visa-on-arrival route to include **Kenya** and **South Africa** (along with Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand and the Philippines).

For ordinary Kenyan and South African passport holders, the current ICP 60-day service requires a valid visa/residence permit/US Green Card from the US, EU or UK, or a valid residence permit from Japan, South Korea, Australia, Canada, Singapore or New Zealand. The passport must be valid for at least 6 months. The stay is 60 days and the visa is non-extendable.

Official sources checked 2026-10-06:
- ICP announcement (25 Jun 2026): https://icp.gov.ae/media-center/icp-expands-eligibility-for-uae-entry-visa-for-nationals-of-certain-countries/
- ICP 60-day service terms: https://icp.gov.ae/en/services-details/?serviceid=68f5bcdb8c587a0011cb16d5

The current `KE → AE` and `ZA → AE` records do not capture this conditional route. My patch will keep the existing base policy intact and add the new conditional eligibility in notes/source metadata rather than incorrectly marking all Kenyan or South African passports as unconditional visa-on-arrival.

Please consider providing a homebrew package for easy installation and especially for easy updating.

### Why it matters

recall is a relatively new project, I'm sure there are many enhancements still left to be discovered or fleshed out, so staying up to date with the latest releases in a convenient way is important to me.
I personally find this more convenient than in-app auto updates.

The knowledge-graph step opens with the user's node in view and most linked nodes outside the panel, so the "what I know about you" moment shows a name and lines going off-screen. Springs rest at 1500 units (the camera distance is also 1500), nodes start in a random 1000-unit cube, the step zooms to 0.72, and nothing fits the graph to the panel. Reproduced on the iOS Simulator with the real `OnboardingKnowledgeGraphStep` and a 5-node graph.

**Product impact** (see [PRODUCT.md](https://github.com/BasedHardware/Omi/blob/main/PRODUCT.md) and [ISSUE_TRIAGE_GUIDE.MD](https://github.com/BasedHardware/Omi/blob/main/ISSUE_TRIAGE_GUIDE.MD))

- Primary loop layer: UX-Polish
- [ ] Involves data loss, failed capture, or broken sync/trust.

**Describe the bug**

Every user who reaches the step with a few memories sees it; it is the payoff screen of the introduction.

**To Reproduce**

1. Finish the voice introduction (a few memories and a goal).
2. "Here is what I know about you" opens.
3. Most nodes are off the panel; you have to pinch or rotate to find them.

**Current behavior**

Initial framing clips most of the graph.

**Expected behavior**

The step fits the graph's bounds to the panel on open (or uses a rest length suited to small graphs).

**Screenshots**

<img src="https://github.com/Itaxh1/omi/blob/pr-assets/onboarding-o07-graph-nodes-offscreen.png?raw=true" alt="The graph step with 4 linked nodes, mostly outside the panel" width="220">

*A 5-node graph (Sam + 4 linked memories) right after the step opens. Real `OnboardingKnowledgeGraphStep`, iOS Simulator.*

**user ID (can we access the user info to validate the bug?):**

Not needed: found in the code; reproduced without a user account where noted.

**Smartphone + device (please complete the following information):**

- Device: iOS Simulator, iPhone 16 (reproduction); shared Flutter code, so physical phones are affected too
- OS: iOS 18.0 (Simulator)
- App Version: `main` at cf8201c2f5 (dev flavor)
- Device version: not involved

**Additional context**

*Root cause.* [Spring rest length 1500](https://github.com/BasedHardware/omi/blob/cf8201c2f532bacb24dfcd4f19412cf26b386e47/app/lib/pages/memories/widgets/memory_graph_page.dart#L155-L157), random start positions within 1000 units ([`memory_graph_page.dart:506`](https://github.com/BasedHardware/omi/blob/cf8201c2f532bacb24dfcd4f19412cf26b386e47/app/lib/pages/memories/widgets/memory_graph_page.dart#L506)), [onboarding zoom 0.72](https://github.com/BasedHardware/omi/blob/cf8201c2f532bacb24dfcd4f19412cf26b386e47/app/lib/pages/onboarding/knowledge_graph_step.dart#L39), perspective camera at 1500 ([`memory_graph_page.dart:950`](https://github.com/BasedHardware/omi/blob/cf8201c2f532bacb24dfcd4f19412cf26b386e47/app/lib/pages/memories/widgets/memory_graph_page.dart#L950)), and no bounds-fitting pass.

*Reproduction.* Reproduced on the iOS Simulator (iPhone 16, iOS 18.0) with a temporary integration test on `main` at `cf8201c2f5` that pumps the real widgets named above; only the network (a local fixture backend) and the pendant/BLE side are faked (the graph comes from a local server):

```
OMI_FACT:o07:graphRequests=1 nodesServed=5 edgesServed=4
```

*Suggested fix.* After the initial layout ticks, compute the bounding box and set zoom/camera so all nodes fit with padding.

Related: #19237 (the same step showing "No knowledge graph yet" to new accounts); this issue is about framing when there is data.

*Part of a review of the first-run flow (sign-in → consent → … → voice introduction → graph → pairing → pendant tutorial); each claim was checked against the code a second time before filing.*

  amount pays the full remainder; prisoner can self-pay; contribution

  bounty-capture fine first, then the rest of their debt
  (oldest-first). `BountyService.payBail` delegates to
  `DebtService.contribute`.
- Books/receipts: the prisoner gets a contribution-credit book (who
  paid, how much, toward which fine, new remaining); the contributor
  gets a chat receipt.
- Refusals: nothing owed, invalid amount, insufficient coins — keyed +
  remedy line, RO+EN lang entries.

**Description:**

In 2026, agentic memory has a dirty secret: **your agent's memories are trapped.** Every memory platform stores your agent's accumulated knowledge — learned preferences, resolved contradictions, hard-won context — in its own proprietary schema. Switch tools, and it all evaporates. Your agent starts over with amnesia.

We believe agentic memory should belong to *you*. That's why Memanto ships with a full migration and portability toolchain, built on the **[Open Knowledge Format (OKF)](https://docs.memanto.ai/integrations/okf)** — Google Cloud's open, vendor-neutral spec for knowledge as plain markdown. With Memanto today you can already:

- **Migrate in** from Mem0, Letta, or Supermemory with a single command: [`memanto migrate`](https://docs.memanto.ai/cli/migrate/migrate) — complete with dry-run previews and token/latency/storage savings reports
- **Export out** to a portable, git-friendly, human-readable OKF bundle: `memanto memory export --okf`
- **Import any OKF bundle** losslessly: `memanto migrate okf ./bundle` — unmapped fields are preserved, nothing is lost
- **Sync** a browsable memory wiki into any project: `memanto memory sync --okf`

The tools exist. What the world hasn't seen yet is the **movement**. We want the open-source community to show every agent builder — vividly, virally, with real data — what it looks like to *escape lock-in and own your memory*.

### **The Challenge:**

Build a **compelling, reproducible migration showcase** that takes memories from another tool into Memanto and out again as portable OKF — proving the full freedom loop: **in → owned → portable**.

⚠️ **Do NOT reinvent the wheel.** The `memanto migrate` CLI and OKF export/import are shipped and documented. Your job is to build *on top of* them — real-world showcases, new migration paths for tools we don't support yet, and creative OKF workflows. Submissions that re-implement what the CLI already does will score poorly on engineering value.

### 💡 Pick Your Path (or Invent Your Own):

- **Path A: The Real-World Escape (Supported Providers)**

    Build (or use) a genuinely lived-in agent on Mem0, Letta, or Supermemory — weeks of evolving preferences, corrections, contradictions. Run `memanto migrate` on it. Show the savings report. Export to OKF. Then prove the round trip: same questions before and after, zero amnesia.

  * *The Goal:* The definitive "switching costs are dead" demo — before/after recall parity plus hard token/latency/storage numbers straight from the migration report.

- **Path B: The New Frontier (Unsupported Sources)** ⭐ *highest engineering value*

    Build a **new migration adapter** for a source we don't support yet — Zep/Graphiti, Hindsight, LangMem, LangGraph checkpoints, or exported ChatGPT/Claude conversation memory. Your adapter should transform the source into either a provider-style export JSON consumable by `memanto migrate --file`, or directly into a valid OKF bundle consumable by `memanto migrate okf`.

  * *The Goal:* A permanent new migration path merged into `/examples/migrations/` that future users can run against their own data. The ChatGPT/Claude angle in particular — "liberate the memory your assistant has built about you" — has massive viral potential with everyday users, not just developers.

- **Path C: The OKF Renaissance (Portability Workflows)**

    Show what becomes possible *once* memory is portable markdown: a git-versioned memory wiki with meaningful diffs across sessions, an OKF viewer/diff utility, a team workflow where agents and humans read the same synced bundle, or a multi-source consolidation where two migrated stores merge into one coherent OKF export.

  * *The Goal:* Make people *feel* why an open at-rest format changes everything — memory you can read, version, review, and carry anywhere.

### **⚙️ Prerequisites:**

- Grab your free Moorcheh API key at **[moorcheh.ai](https://moorcheh.ai/)** — it powers Memanto's serverless retrieval engine. (if you are genuinely working and ran out of free Moorcheh credits, don't worry message us on discord)
- Read the shipped tooling docs before you write a line of code:
  * [`memanto migrate` CLI reference](https://docs.memanto.ai/cli/migrate/migrate) — providers, options, dry runs, savings reports, OKF import behavior
  * [OKF integration guide](https://docs.memanto.ai/integrations/okf) — bundle layout, field mapping, round-trip semantics, `--split` modes

### **🛠️ Implementation Guidelines:**

- **Real Data, Not Toy Data:** Source memories must come from an actual run of the source tool or a genuine exported archive — not hand-written JSON pretending to be a migration. Include the scripts used to generate/populate the source store so the entire pipeline is reproducible end-to-end.

- **Leverage the Shipped Tooling:** Use `memanto migrate` (with `--dry-run` previews and `--report` savings reports) and `memanto memory export --okf` as your backbone. New adapters (Path B) should *feed* the CLI, not bypass it.

- **Fidelity Evidence:** Include the migration summary (source records → mapped memories → per-type breakdown) and, for Path B, a mapping table showing how source-tool concepts (facts, edges, episodes, blocks…) map onto Memanto memory types and OKF fields.

- **Round-Trip Validation:** Include a validation step (LLM-as-a-judge or golden Q&A set) that queries the agent *before* migration (on the source tool) and *after* (on Memanto) and scores recall parity.

- **OKF Artifact Included:** Your PR must include a sample exported OKF bundle that is valid, complete, and human-inspectable.

- **Demo Video Required:** Static screenshots are not enough. Your showcase must include a **demo video** (screen recording) walking through the live migration end-to-end — the source tool losing its memory, `memanto migrate` running, the savings report, the OKF bundle opening as readable markdown, and the agent answering correctly after migration. Any length and style is fine (a tight 2-minute cut often travels furthest), but it must show the real pipeline running, not slides.

- **Total Reproducibility:** Plug-and-play setup — `requirements.txt` or `pyproject.toml`, clear environment variable configuration, a single-command run script, and a README a stranger could follow in under 15 minutes.

### **📊 Judgment Method (The Success Matrix):**

Submissions are scored on a 100-point matrix split between **Engineering Value** and **Social Amplification**.

| Criteria | Max Points | How it is Measured |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Migration Value & Fidelity** | 30 pts | Does the showcase extend beyond what ships today (new adapters and workflows score highest)? Is real data used? Does round-trip validation prove recall parity? Are savings reports and mapping tables complete and honest? |
| **OKF Portability Story** | 15 pts | Is the exported bundle valid and human-inspectable? Does the demo genuinely showcase ownership and portability — not just a file dump? |
| **Reusability & Cleanliness** | 20 pts | Can this merge into `/examples/migrations/` as-is? Clear docs, clean code, single-command reproducibility, passing lint. |
| **Use Case & Storytelling** | 10 pts | Does the demo tell a compelling "own your memory" story (lived-in source data, visceral before/after proof) rather than a trivial transfer? |
| **Social Virality** | 25 pts | Measured via public engagement metrics by the end of the bounty deadline. |

`Social Points = (X Bookmarks × 5) + (X Retweets × 3) + (X Likes × 1) + (YouTube Views ÷ 100) + (YouTube Likes × 2) + (LinkedIn Reactions × 2) + (LinkedIn Comments × 3) + (LinkedIn Reposts × 4)`
